why: A record of truth declared APPEND-ONLY by its door is a plain JSON file any caller can overwrite. The door enforces append-only and the ratified eight fields; nothing enforces that the door is used. A hand-write destroys a proof's whole seal history silently and permanently (Law 7), and looks exactly like a fresh seal.

occurrences.identity: cairn/devices/tester/validation_store.py:79 _atomic_write / :94 persist_validation — declared 'The single write-door' (module docstring line 21) with no physics making it single
occurrences.location: cairn/devices/tester/validation_store.py:94; bypassed from a caller at cairn/ (an ad-hoc sealing script during ticket watchme-emits-a-probe, 2026-07-30)
occurrences.code: v.write_text(json.dumps(rec, indent=2) + '\n')   # rec is ONE validation dict; the file holds a LIST
occurrences.expected: A VALIDATION APPENDS to the trail beside its proof. persist_validation(rec, proof_path=...) reads the existing trail, appends, atomically writes back — so re-running a proof adds a dated seal and never replaces one (validation_store.py docstring: 'There is no update-in-place and no delete, because a record of truth has neither').
occurrences.actual: The bypassing write replaced the whole list with a single bare dict. cairn/tools/base/validations/test_transitions.json went from a 14-entry trail to one dict; cairn/machines/chart/validations/test_chart_verdict.json from 3 to one. SEVENTEEN SEALS DESTROYED, including every seal from every prior voyage of those two components. No error, no warning: the file was still valid JSON and still named after its proof.
occurrences.fatality: NON-FATAL AND SILENT — recovered only by luck of timing. The damage was uncommitted, so `git checkout HEAD -- <paths>` restored both trails (verified: 14 and 3 entries back). Had it been committed, the trails were gone from the working tree and recoverable only by someone who knew to go looking in history for a loss nothing reported. NOTHING detected it: not the door, not a proof, not the tester. It was caught by a human-style double-take on an unrelated AttributeError ('list object has no attribute get') raised by a re-run loop that expected the OLD shape — i.e. the surviving correct files objected, not the corrupted ones.
occurrences.trace: TesterDevice.run_proof(p, isolation='netns') -> returns the 8-field record, and DOES NOT PERSIST (device.py:145, 'the store is a later stone') -> caller must choose the sink -> caller wrote the file directly instead of calling persist_validation -> _atomic_write never reached -> read_validations never reached -> trail replaced. The gap is exactly at the handoff run_proof deliberately leaves open.
occurrences.measured_convention: 57 of 57 files under cairn/*/validations/ are lists — the append-only shape is universal and unbroken across the system, which is why a bare dict is unambiguously corruption and not a second legal shape.
occurrences.owning_ticket: CairnCommons/tickets/charter-state-history-split.json — validation_store.py's own docstring names it (child b). CLAUDE.md 'Rules awaiting physics' already carries the sibling residue for state/history: 'an in-place edit of history itself'. This is the same residue on the third record of truth, now with a measured live occurrence instead of a hypothesis.
occurrences.the_fix_when_taken: Not designed here (this reports, it does not design). The shapes worth weighing: (a) a read-side conformance tooth in the tester's own proofs that reds when any cairn/*/validations/*.json is not a list of eight-field records — cheap, catches it one layer late but LOUDLY, and would have fired here; (b) run_proof persists through the door itself, closing the handoff rather than guarding it, which changes 'the store is a later stone' into a decision; (c) filesystem-level ownership, the expensive answer. (a) is the cheapest thing that would have caught this exact occurrence.
occurrences.found_how: Caught live during ticket watchme-emits-a-probe's sealing step, by the builder who caused it, before commit.

cleared_by.what_changed: cairn e87c386, ticket validation-store-door-is-the-only-path. The declared single write-door is now the only path by physics, in three layers, each answering a different failure mode. (1) MODE BIT: _atomic_write drops a written trail to 0444, so the exact bypass recorded in this ticket — v.write_text(json.dumps(rec)) from an ad-hoc script — now raises PermissionError at the open() instead of destroying 17 seals silently. The door still writes because os.replace needs the DIRECTORY, not the file. (2) CHAIN: every record carries a trail_link minted by persist_validation and by nothing else (a caller-supplied link is refused), a sha256 over the whole trail beneath it plus the record itself; standing() verifies before reading any verdict and refuses the whole trail on a break, so harbor_master clears no crossing on a trail written around the door. This is what answers the sentence at the heart of this ticket — a hand-write no longer looks exactly like a fresh seal. (3) CORPUS SCAN: a proof tooth censuses every module for a write aimed at a validations/ address, so a second writer reds on arrival rather than after it has run. The 73 pre-existing trails were adopted (220 entries linked, all verify); adoption refuses to re-link a tampered trail. WHAT IS STILL TRUE AND IS NOT CLAIMED FIXED: the bytes remain writable to a caller running as the same uid, nothing here can un-destroy a trail (git is the recovery path, and the chain is what tells you to use it), and git carries only the exec bit — so a fresh clone lands these files at 0644 and the mode-bit layer is absent until the door next appends. The chain is the half that survives a clone. Proven: cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_validation_store.py 9/9 (6 new teeth, including both halves of the ticket falsifier — the naive write cannot land bytes, and the forced write cannot pass for a seal), test_quorum 9/9, corpus at 86 proofs · 85 green · 1 red over four consecutive runs.

drained_to.why: troubles/ is a pre-ticket inbox, not a parallel place work lives; a trouble that never becomes a ticket is a bug with no workflow. This record STAYS — it is the account of the live symptom; the ticket is what moves through the gates. Standing does not change here: the trouble clears when the work does.
